en: That was CRUD. Now let's talk about the MVC
pattern, or MVC architecture, which we could
also call it.
MVC stands for Model View Controller,
and in the end, it's just a way of
organizing your files and your code such
that you separate it in a logical and kind
of standardized way,
making it easy for you but also for other
developers to understand edit, read, and
basically work with your code.
So it's basically a pattern which we use,
especially of course for bigger
applications, which ensures that all our
code is always easy to understand and to
maintain. That's the core reason. You don't
need to
use it for technical reasons. You don't need
to use this pattern if you're working on
your own and you love a different setup. If
you wanna have all your code in one file and
you're the only one working with it and
that's fine for you, You can absolutely do
that. But to organize your code for bigger
projects, bigger teams, and simply more
lines of code, the Model-View-Controller
architecture can be helpful.
Now, what is it all about and how does it
work?
Well, let's have a look at these 3 building
blocks, models, views, and controllers. And
let's start with models.
Models simply are constructs in your code
that represent your data. You use models to
manage your core data. For example, in our
example here,
we have our course goals and a course goal
would be a model. So all the logic related
to managing course goals, creating a goal,
fetching goals, updating goals,
all that logic would go into our course goal
model.
We then also have views and we actually also
already have a folder that we named views.
Therefore, it's easy to guess what views are
all about. Views are your HTML files or
templates present your results to the user.
So what you send back to the user, that are
your views.
So in our example, that would be the HTML
files that show a list of course goals, that
show the forms for editing, and so on. These
templates are our views.
And the controller, well, that's between the
models and the views. Controllers basically
connect models to views. Controllers are
responsible for working with the models to
store data, to get data, and for handing
that data off to the views thereafter. So
for example, here we could use the course
goal models to fetch goals and pass that
data to a fitting template.
That's how this pattern works.
Now let's apply it to our project here.
